priced_in_summary: Not a data-center-thesis call; a generic valuation-overshoot call that happens to sit on this chain's link. The method's TOO_LATE test asks whether the decomposition shows multiple expansion eating the runway, and here it shows the extreme opposite: trailing P/E fell from roughly 41.5x to roughly 15.6x over the past year even as FY2025 net income grew 39.65%, driven by two dated, disclosed, real events (the November 2025 FY2025 Q4 miss and guidance cut, then the August 2026 $337 million Construction Management charge) rather than by a slow narrative unwind. That rules out TOO_LATE outright. What the price does ask for, on the market's own near-horizon-invariant reverse-DCF read, is almost no real free-cash-flow growth: 2.4% at the filed snapshot, roughly 1.7% at today's actual close. This dive's own three-scenario rebuild (bear 3.0%, base 10.6%, bull 19.3% FCF-CAGR-equivalent, all built from the company's own disclosed guidance, backlog and margin trajectory) finds the bear case ALONE already above the market's ask, at every scenario examined, which has not happened on any prior name in this log. Set against that: this is the first dive in the log built on a chain link with zero company-specific revenue attribution, sitting instead on a shared four-firm market-share statistic, and on a company that has surprised the market negatively twice within about ten months, including six months after its own board-level decision (February 2026) to retain the exact legacy business line that then produced this quarter's charge. The honest verdict is INVESTABLE: a real, disclosed, bounded overshoot with a margin of safety that survives this dive's own bear case, priced by a market that has been right to be cautious about this name recently and may still be right that more surprises are coming from the wound-down-but-not-yet-exited Construction Management line — which is exactly what no_entry_above and the independence test's falsification condition are for.

independence_test.largest_disagreement: The market, at today's actual price, is pricing AECOM's forward free cash flow to grow at roughly 1.7% a year in perpetuity (2.4% at the filed snapshot price), while even a deliberately conservative rebuild of the company's own disclosed figures — 3% revenue growth (well under the achieved 7.07% trailing 3-year CAGR and under the design segment's still-growing net service revenue), operating margin held flat at the FY2025 level with no further expansion credited, and cash conversion held at FY2025's own already-below-five-year-average ratio — implies roughly 3.0%, and a base case using the company's own guided margin trajectory and record backlog implies roughly 10.6%. The market is asking for less growth than even a skeptical read of AECOM's own numbers would defend.
independence_test.why_the_gap_exists: Recency and segment-contagion bias following two dated, disclosed negative surprises within about ten months (the November 2025 FY2025 Q4 miss and guidance cut, and the August 2026 $337 million Construction Management charge) has pushed the market to price AECOM's entire forward cash-generation capacity as though it carries the estimation and execution risk of one long-duration legacy contract, rather than pricing the design/consulting core (record backlog, +13% year over year, 1.6x book-to-burn, design-segment NSR still growing 4-5%) on its own merits. The category of error is extrapolating a bounded, single-project, single-legacy-segment loss onto a business the company has spent six years actively de-risking: AECOM sold its Management Services business in 2020 and its Civil construction and Power construction businesses in 2021, and this quarter's charge is explicitly on a contract 'awarded in 2019 under terms and conditions that would not be acceptable' under the risk policies the company adopted afterward. This valuation disagreement does not depend on the data-center-moratoria occurrence at all: the gap-table build above rests entirely on company-wide backlog, margin and cash-conversion figures, none of them data-center-specific, so a future contract that quantifies AECOM's data-center-permitting exposure would be a new catalyst the market has not priced, not evidence the current gap is already closed by it.
independence_test.falsification: Stated to prove this dive WRONG, not to confirm it. At the FY2026 Q4 release (expected mid-to-late November 2026, inside review_by), if design-segment net service revenue growth (the metric the Q3 FY2026 release itself broke out separately from the Construction Management line, at 4-5% this quarter) falls below 3% year over year, that would show the erosion is spreading into the design business this dive actually defends, not staying contained to the legacy Construction Management segment, and would undercut the 'bounded, legacy-only problem' reading this dive's independence claim rests on. A single-legged test deliberately: an in-line outcome (design NSR growth staying at or above the 4-5% already reported) tests the dive rather than confirming it by construction.

earnings_quality.basis: Every mechanically computable input is clean, but two real, disclosed, recent negative surprises keep this off a clean A. Accruals: -3.65% of average total assets in FY2024 and -2.14% in FY2025, both well inside the 5% caution band and in the conservative direction (operating cash flow exceeded net income by $425.2 million and $259.8 million respectively). Beneish M-score -2.673 against the -1.78 review threshold, CLEAN, 12 of 12 inputs found. DSO fell across four of the last five fiscal years (71.67, 64.34, 64.59, 63.30, 56.47 days, FY2021-FY2025), the opposite of the sustained-drift flag method section 7 names. Capex to depreciation held in a 0.60x-0.80x band across the same five years (0.772, 0.802, 0.601, 0.669, 0.777), no capex holiday. Cash conversion (operating cash flow over net income) is 1.4625x, well above the 90% grade-A floor. Piotroski is 7 of 9, STRONG, missing only d_leverage and asset_turnover, capital-structure and efficiency notes rather than named section-7 veto inputs. The one deferred-revenue-adjacent input recovered this run (current unearned revenue, from a secondary aggregator since no primary 10-K balance sheet is stored on disk) fell 16.18% FY2024 to FY2025 ($1,298M to $1,088M) after rising 9.17% FY2023 to FY2024 ($1,189M to $1,298M): one down year following one up year, not a sustained multi-year drift, named plainly rather than smoothed over. TWO REAL FLAGS, both disclosed rather than hidden, are why this is B and not A: (1) the FY2025 Q4 release (reported November 2025) missed expectations across the board (net income -22% YoY for the quarter, operating cash flow -34%, adjusted free cash flow -51%), triggering a guidance reset and a roughly 26% stock decline in under a month; (2) this quarter's $337 million pre-tax charge on a Construction Management project 'awarded in 2019 under terms and conditions that would not be acceptable' under AECOM's current risk policies, disclosed with full non-GAAP reconciliation and litigation to recover costs (management cites favorable initial rulings), but arriving only six months after AECOM's own February 2026 strategic review concluded the Construction Management business should be RETAINED rather than sold. Neither flag is Beneish-breach- or channel-stuffing-shaped (no mechanical input above points to manipulation), which is why this does not reach grade C, but two disclosed negative estimate or guidance surprises within ten months is more than 'no flags', hence B.

Two (PRICED_IN_CHECK, ENTRY_BASIS_STRESS) AMENDED the file: a stale-data correction (the market file refreshed since DRAFT time, now solving directly at today's price) and a material completeness gap (the DRAFT never quoted or weighed AECOM's own guided ~56% FY2026 FCF decline). Both amendments, on balance, leave the thesis intact rather than reversing it: the corrected market-implied ask (1.66%) is if anything LOWER than the DRAFT's own hand-derived estimate (roughly 1.7%), widening rather than narrowing the gap, and the guided FCF trough is both already priced (disclosed four weeks before the reference price) and explicitly bounded by the company's own primary-source language ('cash flow excluding the impact of the Construction Management project remains strong'). The pre-mortem is answerable in three genuinely distinct ways (a confirming Q4 print read negatively rather than as already-priced; a second legacy-contract charge; sector-wide multiple compression the reverse-DCF's fixed discount rate cannot see), so this is not downgraded on the pre-mortem test.
red_team.surviving_bear_case: The market has marked AECOM down twice in ten months for real, disclosed reasons -- a November 2025 guidance-cut and, in August 2026, a $337 million charge on a legacy Construction Management contract that also cut FY2026 free-cash-flow guidance to roughly $300 million, about 56% below the $684.9 million FY2025 base this entire valuation is built on -- and the same business unit management chose to retain after a February 2026 strategic review is the one that produced this quarter's charge six months later. This dive's own reverse-DCF read finds even a deliberately conservative bear case (3% revenue growth, flat margin, flat cash conversion) implies more free-cash-flow growth than the market is currently asking for, but that comparison smooths over the one year management has actually guided, and says nothing about whether a second legacy-contract surprise or a sector-wide re-rating of the required return is coming. The thesis is a bet that two real, disclosed, project-specific setbacks are the whole story and that the design/consulting core (record backlog, growing NSR) is being priced as though it carries the same risk as one wound-down legacy line; if a third surprise lands, or if the market's own multiple compression across the whole engineering-consulting peer group continues independent of AECOM's own numbers, that bet is wrong regardless of how cheap the reverse-DCF makes the stock look today.
